newsitem.title: JAPAN: Japan PM may cancel Asia trip over Peru crisis.
newsitem.headline: Japan PM may cancel Asia trip over Peru crisis.

text.p: Japanese Prime Minister Ryutaro Hashimoto may call off a tour of five Southeast Asian countries in January if the hostage crisis in Peru is not resolved, Foreign Ministry officials said on Thursday.
Hashimoto was scheduled to visit Malaysia, Indonesia, Vietnam, Singapore and Brunei between January 7 and 14. All are members of the Association of Southeast Asian Nations (ASEAN).
The officials said they did not know when Hashimoto would announce a formal decision to cancel his trip.
More than 100 hostages remain confined in the Japanese ambassador's residence in Lima by armed Marxist guerrillas, who stormed the residence on December 17.
Separately, Foreign Minister Yukihiko Ikeda may also cancel a scheduled trip to Britain and India early next month, the ministry officials said.
Ikeda has already scrubbed a two-day trip to South Korea that was supposed to start on Friday.
Ikeda reaffirmed on Thursday that the Japanese and Peruvian governments had agreed to make efforts to seek a peaceful end to the hostage crisis.

"The Japanese and Peruvian governments are in complete agreement to seek a peaceful end to the situation, without harm to the hostages. We appreciate the Peruvian government's efforts," Ikeda told a parliament session.
"I cannot speak of the possibility of an end to the hostage situation because any such information might work against our efforts to seek such a resolution," Ikeda said.
